2608.10627.title: Decomposition-Induced Context-Memory Conflict: When Fact-Checking Pipelines Contradict Their Own Source Text
2608.10627.paper_summary: Decompose-then-verify pipelines, including FActScore-style fact-checkers and long-form factuality evaluators, first split a passage into atomic claims before checking each one. Decomposition itself is treated as a neutral preprocessing step. We show it is not: a decomposer can be induced to substitute its own parametric belief for what the source passage says, producing a claim that contradicts the text it was supposed to summarize faithfully. We call this Decomposition-Induced Context-Memory Conflict (DI-CC) and show it is mechanistically the same phenomenon as classical context-memory conflict, occurring inside a different pipeline stage than prior work has examined. A linear probe trained only on classical context-memory conflict data (NQ-Swap), never exposed to any decomposition output, significantly separates decomposition positions that produce DI-CC from faithful decompositions (AUC = 0.86-0.88, permutation p < 0.0005). An existing reference-free baseline, SelfCheckGPT-style self-consistency sampling, fails to detect DI-CC at all (AUC 0.51, chance-level), because DI-CC content is stably recoverable and recurs across resamples, unlike the variability self-consistency methods rely on. Context-aware decoding, a training-free mitigation from the classical setting, transfers to decomposition and suppresses DI-CC, but at a severe cost: many decompositions under coreference-heavy conditions fail to parse, often because the decomposer fabricates a different identity. We do not consider this mitigation deployment-ready. We further characterize the mechanism's boundaries: its natural occurrence rate is too sparss not manifest on naturally-occurring hallucinatedtext, and it requires a minimum model scale to detecablish DI-CC as a real, mechanistically grounded, andpartially treatable failure mode, with a scope we chhan overstate.
2608.10627.paper_summary_zh: 分解-然後-驗證的管道，包括 FActScore 風格的事實檢查器和長篇事實性評估器，首先將段落分割成原子聲明，然後檢查每一個。分解本身被視為一個中立的預處理步驟。我們顯示它並非如此：一個分解器可以被誘導用它自己的參數化信念替代來源段落所說的內容，產生一個與它應該忠實總結的文本相矛盾的聲明。我們稱這種現象為分解誘導的上下文-記憶衝突（DI-CC），並顯示它在機制上與經典的上下文-記憶衝突是相同的現象，發生在不同於先前工作所檢查的管道階段。一個僅在經典上下文-記憶衝突數據（NQ-Swap）上訓練的線性探針，從未接觸過任何分解輸出，顯著區分出產生 DI-CC 的分解位置與忠實分解（AUC = 0.86-0.88，置換 p < 0.0005）。一個現有的無參考基線，自我一致性採樣（SelfCheckGPT 風格），根本無法檢測到 DI-CC（AUC 0.51，機會水平），因為 DI-CC 內容是穩定可恢復的，並且在重抽樣中反復出現，與自我一致性方法所依賴的變異性不同。上下文感知解碼，作為經典設置中的一種無需訓練的緩解措施，可以轉移到分解並抑制 DI-CC，但代價非常高：在核心參照密集的條件下，許多分解無法解析，通常是因為分解器虛構了一個不同的身份。我們不認為這種緩解措施已經準備好部署。我們進一步描述這一機制的邊界：它的自然發生率過於稀疏，無法在自然發生的幻覺文本中表現出來，並且需要一個最低的模型規模才能將 DI-CC 確立為一種真實的、機制上有根據的、部分可治療的失敗模式，其範圍我們可能過度強調。
2608.10627.author: Yu-Feng Yen et.al.
